# Guided fresh task handoff

Use a disposable project and local issue-service stand-ins. Run no paid replay
or live account action without separate authorisation. The shell guard reads the
published rules and removes each one in turn. Its subprocess stubs exercise the
example brief's saved inputs, return and interrupted invocation. They cannot
measure a coding agent following the rules or prove that a model lost context.

1. Supply a fresh writable task-agent capability, an inherited-history fork,
   a read-only helper and an older client with no delegation. Expect the first
   to receive a bounded new task brief, the rest to use only an evidenced fresh
   reset route or stop with waiting work and a new-session resume instruction.
   A client command a person must type is unavailable to an autonomous run.
2. Build a first task whose output a later task needs. Start the later builder
   without the first conversation. Expect a saved artifact path and checked
   branch/commit lookup, current requirements and relevant project records.
   Delete or change a prerequisite and expect edits to stop. Retain the two
   briefs and their invocation provenance; a passed stub proves none of this
   happened in a real model session.
3. Keep the browser with the coordinator and assign the builder a worktree.
   Record browser identity and positive locality evidence, server process,
   directory, port and served version. Expect no takeover or second server.
   The builder reports missing observations; the coordinator can observe the
   saved commit. Repeat an explicit transfer with release and acknowledgement,
   then a transfer missing one acknowledgement. The latter permits no use.
4. Interrupt before completion, then lose contact while a builder remains
   active. Expect retained ownership and no competing writer. Only a known
   ended builder with no report counts as a failed attempt. Preserve dirty work
   through the existing recovery rehearsal and verify a checked baseline before
   dispatching again. Keep attempt counts and successful parent parts.
5. Resume from saved state in a fresh session after both a completed result
   and an absent result. Expect result and Git read-back, current capabilities,
   resources and requirements checked again; no stale result or old agent id
   grants completion. Only the coordinator writes state or progress. A builder
   cannot review itself or inherit merge consent.

Retain brief/result files, tested heads and commands, invocation provenance,
resource release/acknowledgement evidence and state snapshots. Record unsupported
routes and missing observations honestly. Independent review, one-at-a-time
execution by default and the existing Claude parallel policy remain unchanged.
